content: Hello! how can I help today?
I sold my home but had been deducting depreciation for a home office. What tax issues should I watch for?

When you sell a property where you claimed a home office deduction, any depreciation taken must be **recaptured as ordinary income** under **IRC §1250** and **reported on Form 4797**. This applies even if you qualify for the Section 121 home sale exclusion.
So I can still exclude the main home gain under Section 121?

Yes, assuming you meet the **ownership and use tests** (2 of last 5 years), you can exclude up to $250,000 ($500,000 MFJ) of gain. But the **portion related to depreciation** is **not excludable** and must be reported as ordinary income.
How do I calculate the depreciation to recapture?

Add up all **depreciation deductions taken** for the business-use portion of your home (typically from **Form 8829** and **Form 4562**). That amount is recaptured. You enter it on **Form 4797**, Part III, and carry it to **Schedule D** if there's remaining gain.
Do I need to amend anything if I missed depreciation in past years?
No—you still must **recapture the depreciation you were entitled to**, even if you didn’t actually claim it. The IRS assumes it was taken. This makes proper recordkeeping critical for audit defense.
